subject: Greenhouse POC: acceptance gates & metric handoff
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@greenhouselabs.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@greenhouselabs.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Greenhouse POC: acceptance gates & metric handoff

Hi Priya / Tom —

Great to meet today — thanks for the time. This thread is a short post-call recap and a concrete proposal for POC acceptance gates and who owns what. I attached a lightweight spreadsheet (greenhouse_poc_kpis.xlsx) with a suggested metric matrix. Please review and flag anything off.

Call summary (5m):
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for production search-summarization pipeline (100k queries/day target) and reduce cost/token vs current setup.
- Scope for POC: ingest a representative subset (≈200k docs), run 2 evaluation workloads (search-boost + nightly summarization), and measure latency, throughput, cost, and quality.

Proposed acceptance gates (we suggest 3 gating stages):
1) Smoke validation (week 1): successful model load, pipeline end-to-end against 1k queries, no functional errors. Owner: Marissa.
2) Performance gating (week 2–3): p50 latency <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms for the interactive query workload; sustained throughput >= 120 QPS during peak simulation; memory/KV cache behavior stable (no OOM). Owner: Neha.
3) Quality & cost gate (week 3–4): quality benchmark (search relevance NDCG@10 >= 0.62 vs baseline 0.58) and cost/token improvement >= 18% vs current infra. Owner: Diego & Rishi.

Metric definitions (short):
- Latency: p50/p95 measured at service ingress for 512-token average.
- Throughput: sustained RPS during synthetic peak (60s windows).
- Cost/token: fully-loaded token cost including infra + egress, normalized to baseline per-1k tokens.
- Quality: mix of NDCG, exact-match on core intents, and 100 blinded human evals for summarization quality (rubric in sheet).

Next steps / ask for Priya & Tom:
1) Confirm the representative dataset cadence and whether we can get ingestion access by Friday 6/25.
2) Share the critical business queries and 3-5 high-priority evaluation prompts for the summary use case.
3) Note any procurement constraints; I copied procurement@ so we can loop them in.

Attachments: greenhouse_poc_kpis.xlsx (metric matrix) and proposed-poc-timeline.pdf (calendar view).

If this looks good we’ll lock the timeline and run the smoke validation next Tuesday — I’ll assign owners in the playbook.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Greenhouse POC: acceptance gates & metric handoff

Thanks Diego — very clear and helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Dataset access: we can provide a sanitized snapshot (200k docs) but need an NDA addendum for derivative model logs — procurement is copying in to confirm timeline. We can deliver the snapshot by 6/25 if the addendum is quick.
2) Latency targets: our internal SLA for search is p95 <= 300ms on current infra. The p95 <= 400ms you suggested is acceptable as a POC target if p50 shows meaningful improvement. Can we add p99 as an observational metric?
3) Quality: NDCG@10 baseline is 0.60 on our internal eval set — happy to share the eval queries but need to redact any PII first.

We’ll aim to get the sanitized snapshot and 5 representative prompts over the next week. Procurement, can you confirm whether the NDA addendum can be turned in by 6/24?

Looking forward to the smoke validation.

— Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Search & Data Products, Greenhouse Labs
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@greenhouselabs.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@greenhouselabs.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Greenhouse POC: acceptance gates & metric handoff

Thanks Priya — good questions, and yes to adding p99 as observational (we won't gate on it but will report). Updated notes below and immediate owners:

- NDA addendum: Rishi — can you track procurement follow-up?
- Dataset delivery: target 2027-06-25 (Priya deliverable). We’ll provide ingestion instructions and a small S3 bucket for the snapshot.
- Observability: we’ll instrument token-level cost and per-request latency in Kibana/Console; dashboard link will be shared by Monday.

Adjusted acceptance gate thresholds (proposal):
- Performance gate: p50 <= 110ms, p95 <= 350ms (aligned with Priya's baseline), p99 observed.
- Throughput: 120 QPS sustained during a 60s synthetic window (spike test), with error rate < 1%.
- Quality gate: NDCG@10 >= 0.605 (relative improvement of +0.5% acceptable for POC) OR human eval mean score >= 3.8/5 on the provided rubric.
- Cost gate: >15% cost/token improvement vs baseline to pass; 10–15% is a conditional pass with optimization plan.

Proposed timeline (high-level):
- Week 0 (now): legal & dataset scheduling (Priya + Rishi).
- Week 1: smoke validation (Marissa lead) — basic ingestion + 1k queries.
- Week 2: perf tuning & throughput tests (Neha lead).
- Week 3: full eval + human scoring (Marissa + Neha). Decision review and pass/fail.

Action items (owners):
- Priya: confirm dataset delivery by 6/25 and share eval queries.
- Rishi: follow procurement / NDA addendum (target 6/24).
- Marissa: schedule smoke validation run and post-run checklist.
- Neha: prepare perf harness and synthetic peak script; will run baseline vs Redwood.

I’ll draft a short mutual action plan doc and share the dashboard link once instrumentation is ready.

— Diego
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Priya — thanks. Quick logistics from CS side:

- Ingestion: please upload the sanitized snapshot to the S3 link we shared (I’ll re-send instructions). We need sample IDs for 10 target workflows to seed the smoke validation.
- Human eval: we can run the 100-blind evals in parallel with perf tests; I’ll schedule reviewers and a rubric sheet.
- Environment access: we’ll need a service account defined with minimal S3 read permissions + an allowlist IP. Can you confirm the contact for infra on your side?

I’ll put a calendar hold for the smoke validation on Tuesday 6/29 10:00–11:30 PT pending dataset delivery.

— Marissa

Quick internal note / final confirmation before smoke run:

- Dashboard: I published the initial perf dashboard (Console > Trials > GH-4531) — watch p50/p95/p99 and error rate panels. Link: https://console.redwood.com/gh-4531/perf (shared with Priya).
- Test harness: the synthetic peak script will run 10 iterations of a 60s sustained load at 120 QPS; we’ll capture tail latencies and token throughput.
- Cost instrumentation: token accounting will include both model tokens and service overhead. We’ll produce a normalized cost/token sheet post-run.

Confirming the gating thresholds we’ll evaluate against after the run: p50 <= 110ms, p95 <= 350ms, throughput >= 120 QPS with error <1%, NDCG@10 >= 0.605 OR human eval >= 3.8, cost/token improvement >15% to pass.

If the smoke validation looks healthy we’ll schedule a deeper run later in the week to exercise long-tail cases and summarization workload.

— Neha
